def-parabolic-theta-finite-difference-sc:
## Definition

Fix a dimension $d\ge1$, side lengths $L_j>0$, integers $N_j\ge2$, directional diffusivities $\kappa_j>0$, and spacings $h_j=L_j/N_j$. For a finite periodic rectangular grid let
$$
G_h^{\rm per}=\prod_{j=1}^d(\mathbb Z/N_j\mathbb Z),\qquad \langle v,w\rangle_h=\Bigl(\prod_{j=1}^d h_j\Bigr)\sum_{i\in G_h^{\rm per}}v_iw_i,
$$
and define the positive centered heat operator, with indices reduced modulo $N_j$, by
$$(A_h^{\rm per}v)_i=\sum_{j=1}^d\kappa_j\frac{2v_i-v_{i+e_j}-v_{i-e_j}}{h_j^2}.$$

For a two-dimensional Dirichlet rectangle, use the nodes and weighted interior inner product of [[def-rectangular-grid-and-dirichlet-flux-stencil]]. At an interior node $(i,j)$ define
$$(A_h^{B}V)_{ij}=\kappa_x\frac{2V_{ij}-V_{i+1,j}-V_{i-1,j}}{h_x^2}+\kappa_y\frac{2V_{ij}-V_{i,j+1}-V_{i,j-1}}{h_y^2},$$
where values on boundary neighbours are the prescribed Dirichlet row $B$. Write $A_h^0$ for the square matrix on interior values when the boundary is zero. For any boundary vector $B$, let $c_h(B)$ be the result of applying this stencil to the grid vector that equals $B$ on the boundary and $0$ at interior nodes. Then $A_h^B V=A_h^0V+c_h(B)$ on interior nodes.

Let $T>0$, an integer $M\ge1$, $\Delta t=T/M$, $t_n=n\Delta t$, and $\theta\in[0,1]$. Given interior initial data $U^0$, interior source samples $F^n$, and, in the Dirichlet case, boundary rows $B^n$ for $0\le n\le M$ whose time-zero row agrees with the initial grid data, the periodic update is
$$
\frac{U^{n+1}-U^n}{\Delta t}+A_h^{\rm per}\bigl((1-\theta)U^n+\theta U^{n+1}\bigr)=(1-\theta)F^n+\theta F^{n+1},\quad 0\le n<M.
$$
The Dirichlet update, with the boundary values imposed at every time level, is
$$
\frac{U^{n+1}-U^n}{\Delta t}+A_h^0\bigl((1-\theta)U^n+\theta U^{n+1}\bigr)=(1-\theta)\bigl(F^n-c_h(B^n)\bigr)+\theta\bigl(F^{n+1}-c_h(B^{n+1})\bigr),\quad 0\le n<M.
$$
Thus the interior rows use the exact boundary contributions at both endpoints of the time step. The choices $\theta=0,1/2,1$ are forward Euler, Crank–Nicolson, and backward Euler applied to the spatially semidiscrete heat equation; this definition does not redefine those ODE time-stepping procedures.

For a homogeneous-source update with periodic rows or zero Dirichlet boundary values, let $Q_h$ be its one-step linear map when that step is well defined, and give it the operator norm induced by $\|\cdot\|_h$. The family is **grid-norm power stable on $[0,T]$** if there is $C_T<\infty$, independent of the grid and time step, such that $\|Q_h^n\|_{h\to h}\le C_T$ whenever $n\Delta t\le T$. This is a statement in the mesh-dependent finite grid norms defined above.
lem-parabolic-dirichlet-laplacian-is-pos:
## Statement

On the two-dimensional rectangular zero-Dirichlet grid of [[def-parabolic-theta-finite-difference-scheme]], let $A_h$ be the centered positive heat operator with $\kappa_x,\kappa_y>0$. In the weighted grid inner product of [[def-rectangular-grid-and-dirichlet-flux-stencil]], $A_h$ is self-adjoint and positive semidefinite; explicitly,
$$
\langle A_hv,w\rangle_h=h_xh_y\left(\kappa_x\sum_{j=1}^{N_y-1}\sum_{i=0}^{N_x-1}D_xv_{i+1/2,j}D_xw_{i+1/2,j}+\kappa_y\sum_{i=1}^{N_x-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N_y-1}D_yv_{i,j+1/2}D_yw_{i,j+1/2}\right),
$$
so $\langle A_hv,v\rangle_h\ge0$ for every interior grid vector $v$.
lem-periodic-heat-difference-amplificati:
## Statement

On the finite periodic rectangular $d$-grid of [[def-parabolic-theta-finite-difference-scheme]], let $\ell_j\in\{0,\ldots,N_j-1\}$ and
$$
\phi_\ell(i)=\exp\left(2\pi\mathrm i\sum_{j=1}^d\frac{\ell_ji_j}{N_j}\right).
$$
Then $\phi_\ell$ is an eigenvector of $A_h^{\rm per}$ with eigenvalue
$$
\lambda_\ell=4\sum_{j=1}^d\frac{\kappa_j}{h_j^2}\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi\ell_j}{N_j}\right)\ge0.
$$
For zero source, the $\theta$ update multiplies this mode at each step by
$$
g_\theta(\ell)=\frac{1-(1-\theta)\Delta t\lambda_\ell}{1+\theta\Delta t\lambda_\ell}.
$$
The displayed modes form a basis of the complexified grid space, so this factor describes the full periodic update.
thm-parabolic-theta-scheme-local-truncat:
## Statement

Let $\Omega=(0,L_x)\times(0,L_y)$, $T>0$, $N_x,N_y\ge2$, $M\ge1$, $h_x=L_x/N_x$, $h_y=L_y/N_y$, and $\Delta t=T/M$. Let $\kappa_x,\kappa_y>0$, $\theta\in[0,1]$, and suppose $u$ satisfies
$$
u_t-\kappa_xu_{xx}-\kappa_yu_{yy}=f$$
on $\overline\Omega\times[0,T]$, with exact sampled initial and Dirichlet rows in the scheme of [[def-parabolic-theta-finite-difference-scheme]]. Assume $u_{tt},u_{ttt},u_{xxxx},u_{yyyy}$ are continuous on the closed cylinder, and write $M_{tt},M_{ttt},M_{x4},M_{y4}$ for their respective sup norms there. If $r^n$ is the exact grid sample at time $t_n$, the complete interior residual is bounded at every time step by
$$
\|\tau^n\|_\infty\le k M_{tt}+\frac{\kappa_xh_x^2M_{x4}+\kappa_yh_y^2M_{y4}}{12}\quad(\theta\ne\tfrac12),
$$
and
$$
\|\tau^n\|_\infty\le\frac{k^2M_{ttt}}{12}+\frac{\kappa_xh_x^2M_{x4}+\kappa_yh_y^2M_{y4}}{12}\quad(\theta=\tfrac12),
$$
where $\tau^n$ is defined by substituting the exact samples and the exact boundary rows into the fully discrete equation, including its interior rows adjacent to the boundary.
lem-parabolic-theta-step-exists-uniquely:
## Statement

For every finite two-dimensional rectangular Dirichlet grid, $\Delta t>0$, $\theta\in[0,1]$, and interior right-hand side (including the known source and boundary contributions), the θ step of [[def-parabolic-theta-finite-difference-scheme]] has a unique interior solution. Its implicit matrix is $I+\theta\Delta t A_h$, where $A_h$ is the zero-boundary operator.
thm-forward-euler-heat-cfl-and-nyquist-i:
## Statement

On a finite periodic rectangular $d$-grid with $\kappa_j>0$, let $S=\sum_{j=1}^d\kappa_j/h_j^2$. The forward-Euler heat update is nonexpansive in the periodic weighted grid L2 norm whenever $\Delta tS\le1/2$. If every $N_j$ is even, the condition is sharp for that grid family: when $\Delta tS>1/2$, the joint Nyquist Fourier mode has amplification below $-1$ and grows in norm under iteration. At equality its amplification is $-1$, so its magnitude is preserved.
thm-parabolic-theta-l2-stability-for-hal:
## Statement

On a finite two-dimensional rectangular Dirichlet grid with zero boundary data, let $\theta\in[1/2,1]$, $\Delta t>0$, and consider one θ step of [[def-parabolic-theta-finite-difference-scheme]] with source vector $q^n$. It is uniquely solvable and satisfies
$$
\|U^{n+1}\|_h\le\|U^n\|_h+2\Delta t\|q^n\|_h.
$$
In particular, when $q^n=0$ every step is contractive in weighted grid L2. The contraction constant $1$ is independent of the mesh, time step, and number of steps, so this is unconditional finite-time grid-norm stability.
thm-parabolic-theta-scheme-global-error-:
## Statement

Under the smoothness, exact initial data, and exact sampled Dirichlet rows of [[thm-parabolic-theta-scheme-local-truncation-error]], let $\theta\in[1/2,1]$ and let $U^n$ be the fully discrete solution. At every time level $m\le M$,
$$
\|r^m-U^m\|_h\le 2T\sqrt{L_xL_y}\,R_\theta,
$$
where
$$
R_\theta=\begin{cases}kM_{tt}+(\kappa_xh_x^2M_{x4}+\kappa_yh_y^2M_{y4})/12,&\theta\ne1/2,\\k^2M_{ttt}/12+(\kappa_xh_x^2M_{x4}+\kappa_yh_y^2M_{y4})/12,&\theta=1/2.\end{cases}
$$
Here $r^m$ is the exact solution sampled on the grid and $\|\cdot\|_h$ is the weighted interior L2 norm. Thus the global rate is first order in time when $\theta\ne1/2$, second order in time when $\theta=1/2$, and second order in each spatial spacing under the stated derivative and boundary hypotheses.
thm-theta-scheme-discrete-maximum-princi:
## Statement

On the finite two-dimensional rectangular Dirichlet grid of [[def-parabolic-theta-finite-difference-scheme]], suppose $\theta\in[0,1]$, the source is zero, and
$$
\Delta t(1-\theta)\left(\frac{\kappa_x}{h_x^2}+\frac{\kappa_y}{h_y^2}\right)\le\frac12.
$$
Then every numerical interior value at every time level lies between the minimum and maximum of all initial and prescribed boundary values. In particular, with homogeneous boundary rows and $\theta=1/2$, this maximum-principle condition is $\Delta t(\kappa_x/h_x^2+\kappa_y/h_y^2)\le1$, a stricter sufficient condition than the unconditional weighted $L^2$ stability for the same homogeneous problem proved in [[thm-parabolic-theta-l2-stability-for-half-theta]].
